messages.content: Write the introduction to a monthly engineering newsletter whose theme this month is technical debt. Around 200 words.

output:
Clean through the slopwatch gate. Here it is (~205 words):

---

Nobody plans technical debt. It accumulates while you're busy shipping something else.

It's the deploy script only Priya can run. The feature flag from a 2023 experiment nobody will delete. The test that fails on Tuesdays, so we rerun it and move on. None of those were bad calls at the time — they were Thursday afternoons with a release on Friday, and the tradeoff was obvious and correct. The bill just arrives later, in a different currency, and usually while someone new is on call.

So this month we're writing about the things we step over.

Inside: **[NAME]** on why the auth migration took nine months instead of six weeks, and what she'd tell her past self. **[NAME]** argues that some debt should never be paid down at all — mark it, document it, leave it alone. **[NAME]** walks through the dependency audit that turned up 214 packages we haven't imported since 2024.

One ask before you read. Think of the thing in your area you always apologize for in code review. Write it down. Bring it to the retro on **[DATE]**. Ugly work is easier to name out loud than it is alone in a diff.

---

Swap the bracketed placeholders and the three "Inside" teasers for your actual pieces — the nine months, the 214 packages, and Priya's deploy script are stand-ins, and the paragraph only lands if those details are real. If you send me the actual contents list I'll rewrite that middle block to match.
